sentences: We trained on 4631 innings from before 2026 and tested on 515 innings from 2026, which the model had never seen.
The biggest factor was runs scored at the halfway mark: a typical difference of 25.0 runs moves the predicted final total by about 36.5 runs.
Each extra wicket lost at the halfway mark costs about 6.2 runs by the end of the innings, given the other things the model knows.
Adding wickets lost at the halfway mark moved the average miss from 19.7 to 19.3 runs.
Adding runs scored in the powerplay moved the average miss from 19.3 to 19.2 runs.
On average the final model's prediction was 19.2 runs away from the real total, against 20.9 runs for the TV projected score.
The model beat the TV projection by 1.7 runs on average. That is short of the 3.0-run margin we asked for, so we tried every feature we had.
